messages:
Michael: Heads-up — onboarding astra-6b weights. Origin is HF but ownership/namespace is fuzzy.
HF path: https://huggingface.co/org/astra-6b/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin
We need an S3 copy + registry entry. Tokenizer looks weird: BOS token id 5012 that shifts pad behavior in fast tokenizers. Also found checksum mismatch on shard_00002 (expected md5 d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e, got 9c1e5f...). Can someone confirm presign TTL for the mirror job and a quick owner for reupload?

Anya: I can take presign/perm checks. For staging sync I usually use 1h presign TTL, for final mirror use 24h. +1 for registry entry. tagging infra if they need IAM tweaks.

Sam: @Michael can you paste the manifest file? If shard checksum mismatches it's often truncated during upload. Also which IAM role does the mirror runner assume?

Michael: manifest snippet:
```
{ "model": "astra-6b", "shards": ["shard-00001", "shard-00002"], "checksums": ["e3b0c44298fc1c14...", "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"] }
```
IAM role: `arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/s3-mirror-ingest-prod` — that's what the pipeline uses.

Kevin: I can run a head/md5 check from the mirror host. Give me a presign URL or temporarily make the object readable for 15m.

Lisa: Quick note on the tokenizer quirk — tokenizer.json includes `"bos_token_id": 5012` but the training preprocessing used `eos_as_pad=true`. Fast tokenizers treat that differently, causing pad offsets to shift in batched evals. Our loader should enforce `eos_as_pad=False` when converting; I'll add a small compatibility patch in the artifact loader.

artifact-bot: registry:create request received for `astra-6b`. Status: pending. Required: canonical S3 path, manifest with verified checksums, and CI green on registry PR.

Anya: I'll open the registry PR and tag @Kevin for artifact verification. @Michael can you try re-uploading shard-00002 with the following to avoid metadata issues:
`aws s3 cp shard-00002 s3://redwood-artifacts/astra-6b/shard-00002 --no-guess-mime-type --content-type application/octet-stream --acl bucket-owner-full-control`
Sometimes the CLI guesses text encodings and truncates.

Michael: Reuploading now. Ran:
`aws s3 cp shard-00002 s3://redwood-artifacts/astra-6b/shard-00002 --acl bucket-owner-full-control`
Will post back when the job completes.

Kevin: Ran head checks before reupload — size mismatch confirmed. After Michael's reupload sizes match and md5 is clean. artifact-bot: please re-run digest.

artifact-bot: digest re-run complete — checksums matched for all shards. Registry PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/artifacts/pulls/412. Added tags: `needs-tokenizer-note`.

Lisa: I pushed a tiny loader change and a unit test. PR snippet:
```
# loader compatibility fix
if tokenizer.get("eos_as_pad", False):
    tokenizer["eos_as_pad"] = False
```
Ran local eval on a few prompts — padding/alignment issue resolved.

Sam: CI for the registry PR shows one packaging flake (unrelated). @Michael can you set a deploy window for the dedicated mirror (low traffic midnight) so we don't spike telemetry?

Michael: Scheduled mirror job for 02:00 UTC and kicked off final replicate. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Kevin: Verified mirror completed at 02:07 UTC, all checks green.

Anya: I'll merge the registry PR after CI completes and add a short note in the onboarding checklist about the eos/pad quirk.

Michael: Closing the loop — model added to registry, tokenizer loader patch in prod canary. Appreciate the quick turnaround everyone.
